title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 142
paragraphs: So when Alexander had ceased speaking, the envoys from Sparta followed him at once and said: “As for us, the Lacedaemonians sent us to ask of you not to make any change in what concerns Greece, nor to accept proposals from the barbarian — since this is in no way just, nor honorable for any of the Greeks to do, and least of all for you, for many reasons. It was you who stirred up this war, when we by no means wanted it; and the contest came about for your dominion, but now it extends to all of Greece. Besides, it is by no means tolerable that you Athenians, who are the authors of all this, should prove to be the cause of slavery to the Greeks — you who have been known from ancient times as the liberators of many. Still, we feel sympathy for you in your sufferings, because you have been deprived of your crops twice now and have had your substance ruined for a long time. In compensation for this, the Lacedaemonians and their allies offer to support your wives and all members of your households who are unfit for war for as long as this war shall last. But do not let Alexander the Macedonian persuade you by smoothing Mardonius's speech. It is fitting for him to do these things, since being himself a tyrant he is working in league with a tyrant; but for you these things are not fitting, if you are rightly minded. For you know there is neither faith nor truth in barbarians.”
